notes: Corrected: the dummy 'it' of 'neither shall it be for thine honor' was moved out of the resultative lamed's frame into its own added unit. Rule 20 limits the dummy that joins a predicate's unit to the presentative 'there', and rule 49's frames contain no subject pronoun; the clause writes no subject morpheme, so the impersonal 'it' is licensed by nothing — the same ground on which the verse's first 'It' is added. The lamed keeps 'shall ... be ... for', headed on 'for'.
'It' of 'It pertaineth' remains added under rule 20's impersonal-subject sentence; folding it into the possessive lamed's rendering was the competing reading.
The first lamed of lecha is unrepresented because the ASV writes only 'thine' for it and its suffix (rules 18, 40).
'pertaineth unto' was kept whole on the possessive lamed and headed on the English preposition (rule 49).
